I am a woman of 47 years in Phalombe, and this small piece of land is what feeds my family. The rains have been unreliable these past seasons, so I must be careful with every kwacha. I will try to get a little fertilizer through the government subsidy program if my name is on the list, and I always put the manure from my goats on the field before planting. I intercrop my maize with pigeon peas and pumpkins like my mother taught me, and I do the work myself with my children because hiring people is too expensive.
